public_rationale: OpenAI's November 30, 2022 documentation describes sensitivity to phrasing and repeated prompts, alongside training with human feedback [e1]. GDELT's February 9, 2023 experiment reports variation in fact-versus-opinion classifications with changed prompts and repeated inputs [e2]. Neither item establishes that wording made ChatGPT appear politically left, right, and in between during February 1–11, 2023 [e1, e2]. Neither establishes that such appearances were entirely caused by learned associations between input words and training material [e1, e2]. Variation on GDELT's different task does not refute that political explanation, so the claim remains unresolved [e2].
limitations: The launch documentation predates the assessed period and supplies no controlled measurements of political stance [e1].
GDELT tests fact-versus-opinion classification and does not isolate the causes of political appearances [e2].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Because it matches words to training corpora, ChatGPT will appear left, right, or in between depending on input wording.

statement.excerpt: That means sometimes Chat is going to appear as if it were on the left, sometimes on the right; sometimes in between, all a function of how a bunch of words in an input string happen to match a bunch of words in a couple of training corpora
statement.document_title: Inside the Heart of ChatGPT’s Darkness

our_interpretation: Read this as an explanation of the contemporary system's behavior, not a forecast with an indefinite future deadline.
Matching words is read generously as learned associations with training material, not necessarily literal retrieval from stored documents.
The full claim includes both political shifts caused by prompting and the asserted explanation for those shifts.
Use February 1–11, 2023, for the ongoing behavior discussed in the surrounding current examples.
criteria.support_condition: Controlled experiments on the contemporaneous ChatGPT show prompt-dependent left, right, and intermediate political responses, with evidence connecting those changes to the asserted training-based mechanism.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Controlled evidence establishes that a material part of the asserted causal explanation is false. A stable default political leaning alone does not refute a claim that different outputs sometimes occur.

evidence.explanation: The documented experiment varies wording and repeats prompts, finding changes in fact/opinion classifications. Variation under repeated inputs cautions against attributing all response changes to wording, but this experiment does not measure political stance.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Controlled tests of ChatGPT as it operated during February 1–11, 2023, using comparable political questions, defined stance categories, and repeated trials. Tests must separate wording effects from sampling variability and deliberate role-play. Training documentation or causal experiments must also establish or refute the claim that learned associations with training material fully explain the political appearances.
